title: Blurring makes counts hard and keeps failures and composition
claim: Blurring makes counts hard and keeps failures and composition. (1) For a law on D and a surjection phi from D' onto D, the blurred law (each relation replaced by its preimage) has the same failing systems and the same circuits (range-relative constrained sets), so it composes like cycles exactly when the law does, and its count weights each solution of the image system by the sizes of its values' preimages. (2) Every Mal'tsev law on three values composes like cycles: a three-element Mal'tsev algebra has at most one nontrivial congruence (two would make it a product of two two-element algebras), which is KNOT-CIRCUITS Theorem 1's condition; all 531441 Mal'tsev operations on {0,1,2} were checked (530421 simple, one of them affine; 1020 with one congruence of blocks 2+1). (3) Blurred signed parity on three values (0 doubled; the preimages of even and odd parity) is Mal'tsev (exactly the 48 non-simple operations whose quotient is affine preserve it), composes like cycles, has knots, fails recognisably (Gaussian elimination on its image), and its count is #P-complete: the count matrix of its relation has rank 2, so it is not strongly balanced (Dyer-Richerby). So it has mutual selection in PINNING C's sense and composes like cycles: SELECT-COUNT A's exclusion holds exactly on two values. (4) Blurred signed Z3 on four values (0 doubled) is the same in every respect. Checked: the blurring lemma on random systems (failures, circuits, counts), the enumeration, the knots, recognition against brute force, the count matrices, and circuit elimination on random small systems of both blurred laws.
failure_conditions: A blurred system whose failure, circuits or count disagree with its image system's.
A Mal'tsev operation on three elements with two nontrivial congruences.
A blurred-parity or blurred-Z3 system violating circuit elimination.
A count matrix of the blurred relations of rank 1.
foundation_claim_scope: Counting and composition of finite laws on three and four values; mutual selection in PINNING C's formal sense only.
